facts.finding: Scoped canonical inventory identities and source observations exist. Gateway devices are a separate table; inventory relationships require both endpoints to be inventory entities, so a Device ID cannot be inserted as an inventory relationship endpoint without inventing an inventory identity.

Original Device is scoped ID/name/state/version/replay floor; it has no Agent foreign key. Current credentials bind the same scoped Device via original credential/enrollment foreign keys. No Agent admission is implied.

Canonical inventory identity hashes the original scope/entity-kind/source-native identity. Association must retain that identity rather than create an Agent from Device ID, display name, address, or enrollment.

Existing repository Device create takes ID and name only; enrollment issue takes Device ID and original token material. Neither input includes an Agent. Bounded production Go callsite search found their interface/definitions but no connected public handler invocation.
Discovery public handler dispatches existing sync/schedule/freshness/setup operations. It does not provide an Agent-to-Device admission or gateway-device management operation.

Closed operation-target inventory includes typed Agent and selected environment control operations; unknown operations may not borrow environment permission. No gateway-device target mode is declared.

Current authorization80 source registry resolves active typed Agents from inventory. It has no gateway-device source kind. Device must remain native credential/device authority unless a separately reviewed new target contract is implemented.

facts.anchor: -- Device management has a distinct registered API login.
facts.finding: Current gateway_api_organization_lock checks original registered discovery API login and organization serialization. Its comment explicitly excludes replacing HTTP/OpenFGA checks. Native SQL EXECUTE privilege is not sufficient user authority for a new association operation.

Current updateAgent statement gate binds exact current human credential, manage_workflows ceiling, one actual Agent target, closed owner/team/tags input, and selected profile pin. It does not authorize an association by writing a tag, owner string, or arbitrary attribute.

Current ownership profile demonstrates existing proof/revision/identity fences under the original source/API authority. Its exact updateAgent operation and single-target ABI cannot be repurposed for Device association.

Existing OpenFGA identity/workflow/view relations and human organization/environment roles can support an explicitly reviewed new operation without inventing principals. Existing relations do not themselves authorize an unregistered operation or prove physical routing.

Explicit placement-v2 uses authenticated provider collection, double-checked Kubernetes identity/owner facts, original Agent identity and optional observed cluster/controller/Pod/Node UID/boot attributes. These fields contain no gateway Device credential or Agent-to-Device admission.
Placement schema explicitly grants no runtime health, policy coverage or Kubernetes access. A shared node or namespace cannot bind a gateway to every colocated Agent.
Gateway EvaluationEvidence.AgentID is taken from action request attributes. This is event attribution, not a two-sided administrative or workload identity association.

Existing worker runtime ancestry validates current active fresh Agent, correlated session/event evidence and current Device credentials, retaining run-scoped source metadata. Its Agent ID originates from evaluation/session attribution; this cannot establish a persistent installation association or be promoted to one.
Runtime correlator results retain event/session/Agent and optional sandbox/sensor provenance, not an authenticated Device-to-Agent association credential.

New installation testimony is keyed by native scope/Device/credential/generation. It intentionally has no Agent field. Joining it to an Agent requires a separate admitted association and current provenance checks; matching environment alone is insufficient.

recommended_next_connected_design.product_flow: Explicit administrative admission of an existing typed Agent to an existing active native Device and exact current credential generation, plus native Device acceptance. Label as admitted association; expose provenance/freshness/revocation. This is configuration testimony, not observed routing or enforcement.
recommended_next_connected_design.identity: Reuse original scoped Agent ID and selected admitted source-native identity and original native Device ID/credential/generation. Do not create an identity kind, FGA principal, provider credential, inventory Device alias or auto-grant.
recommended_next_connected_design.permission_boundary: Freeze a NEW closed current operation and target policy. A conservative candidate requires fresh-auth human manage_identity on both the existing environment and exact Agent target, with current membership and current active typed-source proof. Both are existing resource/permission forms; however multi-target operation ABI and registered statement/profile still need explicit implementation and review. Existing updateAgent/manage_workflows cannot authorize this mutation and no new permission is assumed admitted by this audit.
two_sided_admission_candidate: Human current-authorized request creates a bounded expiring intent for the exact scoped Agent/source identity and active Device/credential generation, with original authorization/audit provenance and idempotent CAS semantics.

Existing Device credential signs acceptance of the exact stored intent/challenge through the original HTTP proof, without supplying trusted scope or Agent identity of its own. The acceptance is pending evidence only.

Human finalization reauthenticates current Stytch session/current permissions and source identity, verifies current same-generation native Device acceptance, rechecks after lock waits and confirms transaction commit before success. This avoids borrowing or fabricating a stored human request proof inside the native gateway caller.
recommended_next_connected_design.persistence: Additive separately sealed namespace owned by the original registered discovery source authority. Original registered discovery API and gateway-control callers get only exact reviewed functions; FORCE RLS, closed manifests and unexpected/default ACL rejection. Never rewrite immutable SQL14/15/79/80, native identity, original source fingerprints, request grants or device replay floor.
recommended_next_connected_design.source_freshness: Bind the immutable scoped source-native Agent identity and provenance source, record exact admission snapshot/evidence. Current reads must revalidate active/fresh source identity. Freeze whether subsequent same-identity last-good snapshots retain the association rather than invalidating every normal sync; changed UID/source identity never auto-rebinds. Annotation owner/team/tag changes do not authenticate routing.
recommended_next_connected_design.revocation: Explicit association revoke/CAS and source removal/tombstone/freshness loss, Device revoke/delete, credential expiry/rotation and wrong scope must make association unavailable. Old generation cannot silently transfer. Current user permission/session revocation denies new intent/finalization/read immediately via original current authorization. Decide separately whether completed administrative configuration persists after its historical author loses permissions; it must never grant that author ongoing access.
recommended_next_connected_design.multiplicity: Freeze many-Agent-per-Device and multi-Device-per-Agent semantics explicitly. No inferred exclusive, all-instance or fleet claim. Every selected source/device/generation relation needs bounded independent evidence.
recommended_next_connected_design.read_ui: Connect actual current-authorized Agent detail and a bounded association view/mutation UI to typed APIs. Distinguish pending/admitted/revoked/source-stale/device-unavailable/credential-rotated states and show evidence. Do not emit a covered/healthy filter until separate coverage composition and freshness acceptance are complete.
recommended_next_connected_design.scope_limit: Administrative admission plus Device possession does not prove that the Agent workload actually uses that Device. Actual routing/workload identity proof remains a separate required design if the original coverage requirement depends on observed enforcement. No local event attribute, IP, namespace, pod colocation, mutable annotation or policy GET can substitute.

grouped_acceptance_before_implementation: Define all current human/Device/source/permission boundaries together; actual failing grouped application cases before connected implementation where dependencies permit, with setup failures classified honestly.

Discovery same-identity refresh versus source UID replacement, removed/stale Agent, Device revocation/rotation and association CAS/revoke behavior.

Original policy cache refresh, signatures/failure modes, decision floor, approvals/budgets, current authorization and UI typecheck/build remain intact. Native and deployed real-provider/Stytch acceptance stay separately required.
